payload.title: Cities, rivers and mountains of western Europe

explanations.Bordeaux: A port city on the Garonne in south-western France.
explanations.Hamburg: Germany's second-largest city, a port on the Elbe.
explanations.Seville: The capital of Andalusia, in southern Spain.
explanations.Rhine: A great European river that flows north through the German Rhineland.
explanations.Ebro: The longest river lying entirely within Spain.
explanations.Mont Blanc: The highest mountain of the Alps, rising above Chamonix in France.
explanations.Zugspitze: The highest mountain in Germany, above Garmisch-Partenkirchen in Bavaria.
explanations.Mulhacen: The highest mountain in mainland Spain, in the Sierra Nevada.

sources.excerpt: Bordeaux is a city on the river Garonne in the Gironde department, southwestern France.
Hamburg, officially the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, is the second-largest city in Germany after Berlin and sixth-largest city in the European Union, with a population of over 1.9 million.
Seville is the capital and largest city of the Spanish autonomous community of Andalusia and the province of Seville.
The Loire is the longest river in France and the 171st-longest in the world.
After that, the Rhine defines much of the Franco-German border. It then flows in a mostly northerly direction through the German Rhineland.
The Ebro is a river of the north and northeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in Spain.
The three towns and their communes which surround Mont Blanc are Courmayeur in Aosta Valley, Italy; and Saint-Gervais-les-Bains and Chamonix in Haute-Savoie, France.
The Zugspitze, at 2,962 m (9,718 ft) above sea level, is the highest peak of the Wetterstein Mountains and the highest mountain in Germany.
Mulhacén, with an elevation of 3,479 metres (11,414 ft), is the highest mountain in peninsular Spain and in all of the Iberian Peninsula.
